sources.citation: Vogler, Pierre. 2024. La position du kuwaa au sein du groupe kru (Libéria, Niger-Congo). Preprint, HAL hal-04651776, version 1 (deposited 17 July 2024), 13 pp. Illkirch-Graffenstaden.
sources.note: No statement of the Kuwaa tone inventory or tone rules anywhere. Tone appears only (i) as tone marks on cited forms and (ii) in two passing historical remarks: p.4 'En kuwaa, elle etait suivie d'une syllabe qui laisse une trace tonale' (a lost syllable leaving a tonal trace on 'pere') and sec. 8 'glissement du ton sur la modalite postposee' (tone shift explaining the 3SG pronoun form). The paper is lexical/morphological comparison for subgrouping (concludes Kuwaa groups with Bassa-Klao in far-western Kru).

sources.citation: Zogbo, Lynell Marchese. 2012. Kru revisited, Kru revealed. Paper presented for the International Congress 'Towards Proto-Niger-Congo: Comparison and Reconstruction', Paris, 18-21 September 2012. 11 pp. (Glottolog ref 308018; formerly athttp://llacan.vjf.cnrs.fr/fichiers/nigercongo/fichiers/Zogbo-Kru.pdf)
sources.note: Family-level Kru handout: reconstructs four level tones for Proto-Kru ('three to four level tones' across the family, high functional load); says nothing about Kuwaa's own tone system.

tone.quote: *Four level tones, with a few examples of 4 > 3, innovated modulated tones resulting from tone-consonant interaction and consonant voicing; tone carries a high functional load in the lexicon and in the grammar: distinguishing 1-2nd person (sg and pl), perfective-imperfective, negation
tone.locator: p. 4 (unnumbered handout page), section 'PROTO-PHONOLOGY'; cf. p. 1 'three to four level tones' among the family's standard Niger-Congo features
tone.summary: Family-level Kru handout: reconstructs four level tones for Proto-Kru ('three to four level tones' across the family, high functional load); says nothing about Kuwaa's own tone system.
